teaches: The f-pawn's early strike offers a pawn to seize the centre and the initiative. The knight developed to c3 first is what makes it sound — the centre is covered, so whichever way the offer is answered, the pawns and pieces come forward with tempo. Passive declines concede the centre without even winning the pawn.
explains: The pawn on f4 attacks the pawn on e5 and puts the whole game's character on the table in one move. Accepting hands over the centre for a pawn; propping the pawn up with slow moves keeps the material and gives up the initiative instead.

line: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d6 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5
teaches: When a pawn chain's strongpoint is held by a knight, the bishop's pin against that knight is pressure on the strongpoint itself — the defender is frozen, so every attacker you add counts double. Develop toward the pin rather than around it.
explains: The bishop on b5 attacks the knight on c6, the piece holding up the pawn on e5, and the king behind the knight makes the attack a pin. The strongpoint's defence is stretched one move after it was declared.
